sections.name: Owner and executive team
sections.who: Owner / Managing Director and any directors

questions.q: In one sentence, what must the website and app achieve for Justrite in the next 12 months?
What are the three metrics you will check weekly to know it is working?
Which functions go live first and which wait?
Who has the final say on: prices, delivery fees, discounts, refunds, product range, and pausing the online channel?
What spending or commitment limits apply for each approver, and who covers when you are away?
How do you describe Justrite in your own words: the promise, the customers, what makes it different from HealthPlus, Medplus and other chains?
Which words, claims and tones must never appear in our content?
Do you want content in English only, or also Pidgin, Yoruba or Hausa?
Are you willing to have a public LinkedIn profile and be the face of the company? What topics are off limits?
Who should be the third LinkedIn profile (we suggest the Superintendent Pharmacist)? Has that person agreed?
Do you already have a LinkedIn profile or company page? Who owns the company page today? Please give the links.
May we use staff names, photos, and licence numbers publicly? Which ones, with what written consent?
Who approves each content type before publishing?
Which regulators or associations are you a member of or want to be seen with?
Which hospitals, HMOs, employers, suppliers or manufacturers are formal partners we may name publicly?
What is your policy on discounts, loyalty points, free delivery thresholds, price matching and price locks?
Who is responsible for answering the question "is this product genuine?" and what proof will you show?
Do you allow AI crawlers and AI assistants to read the website?
How much of the pharmacy's patient data may we use, in aggregated and anonymous form, for content and press? Under what safeguards?
What is your appetite for public pricing and published promises (delivery fee, delivery time, refund rule)? What would make you withdraw one?
What are your expansion plans for the next 24 months (new stores, states, services) that the website and app must be ready for?
What previous marketing, agency or website work should we know about, including what failed?
Who are the three competitors that worry you most, online or offline?
What would make you stop or pause this programme?
What is the best way and time to reach you for approvals, and who may approve on your behalf?

sections.name: Superintendent pharmacist and pharmacists
sections.who: Superintendent Pharmacist, store pharmacists, reviewing pharmacists

groups.title: Safety rules for content and tools
Adverse events, recalls and stock rules

questions.q: Which medicines may be sold online without a prescription, which only with a reviewed prescription, and which never online? Please share the list or the rule.
How do you classify controlled, restricted and schedule drugs for online and store sales? What documents are required?
What counts as a valid prescription (handwritten, printed, e-prescription, hospital letter)? What details must be present?
Maximum age of a prescription before it needs renewing, by drug type?
Can a prescription be refilled? How many times, how often, and what proof is needed at each refill?
What is the target turnaround for prescription review during opening hours and outside them?
What are the rules for approving, asking for clarification, rejecting, and contacting the prescriber? Please give the steps in order.
What note must the pharmacist record with each decision, and for how long are records kept?
Who covers prescription review when the pharmacist is off, on leave or in a different store? Is cross-store review allowed?
How many pharmacists are available for review, and at which hours? Is there a pharmacist at every store at all opening hours?
When is generic substitution allowed, who decides, and how is the customer told?
Which drug-interaction, allergy and dose-limit checks must happen before dispensing? What do you do when the symptom checker or interaction checker disagrees with your judgement?
Which red-flag symptoms must always send the customer to a doctor or emergency care? Please supply the list we should show on every health tool and article.
Which groups need extra care in content and in the app? (children, pregnancy, elderly, kidney or liver disease)
How should antibiotics, antimalarials, steroids, and pain medicines be handled in content, search and recommendations?
Which health claims may we make, and which are forbidden (cure, prevent, guaranteed, best)?
Who will review every health article, tool page, FAQ and carousel? Names, credentials, PCN numbers, backup reviewer.
How long can you take to review a piece of content, and how many pieces per week can you realistically review?
Which sources do you accept as authoritative?
How often should health content be re-reviewed? Which content is high-risk and needs shorter cycles?
How are adverse events, side effects, wrong medicine, wrong dose and complaints reported, recorded and escalated? Who reports to NAFDAC?
How is a recall or counterfeit alert handled today, step by step? What must the app do (freeze batch, list customers, message them)?
Which batch, expiry and storage details must be recorded at receiving and at dispensing?
What is your minimum remaining shelf-life rule at sale and for delivery?
Which medicines need cold-chain or special storage and delivery, and should they be excluded from online delivery?
What is the status of the Electronic Pharmacy / e-pharmacy registration for Justrite, who leads it, and what is the timeline?
What do you need from the website and app to satisfy an inspection (records, exports, audit trails)? Please give an example of a past inspection request.
May the pharmacist see health data of customers? Which roles may see which data, and what reason must be logged?
What disclaimers do you require on tools, articles and consultations?
How should free pharmacist consultation requests be triaged, answered and documented? Channels, hours, limits, escalation to a doctor?
Do you consent to be named and photographed as the reviewing pharmacist on the website and on LinkedIn? What details may be shown?
What pharmacist posts or comments on LinkedIn would you be comfortable with, and what is off limits (individual advice, product promotion)?
What questions do customers ask you most often? Please list the top 20, with the answer you give.
What is the most common mistake or complaint you want the website to prevent?

sections.name: IT and technology
sections.who: IT lead / Head of IT / current web or hosting provider

questions.q: Who owns the domain justritepharmacy.com and where is it registered? Who holds the registrar login and the DNS?
When does the domain renew and is it set to auto-renew? Is registrar lock on?
Where is the current WordPress site hosted, who administers it, and can we get a full backup and an admin login?
Which email addresses use the domain (for example onlinesales@)? Where is email hosted, and what must not break at cut-over?
Are Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager set up for the domain? Who is the owner of each?
Do you have analytics history for the last 16 months we can export?
Who owns the Google Business Profiles, Facebook page, Instagram, YouTube and any LinkedIn page? Whose email is the account owner? Is two-step verification on?
Where will the new platform be hosted (your own server, a cloud provider, container)? Who administers it and what are the uptime expectations?
Who is the technical contact available at cut-over and for the 14 days after it? Out-of-hours contact?
What is the acceptable downtime window for the DNS switch, and which day and time is best?
Which systems must the website and app connect to?
What POS or inventory system do the 14 stores use? Can it export products, prices, stock, batches and expiry? In what format and how often?
Which payment accounts exist (Paystack, bank accounts, POS terminals)? Who holds the keys, and who may rotate them?
Who owns the WhatsApp Business number and account? Is it verified? Which number should customers see?
Which SMS sender ID and provider do you use or plan to use?
How are staff accounts created, changed and removed today? Who approves access to prescriptions, customer data, refunds and prices?
What password, two-step verification and device rules should staff follow? Are shared logins used anywhere today?
How is customer and prescription data stored, who can export it, and where must it stay (country, provider)?
Is there a Data Protection Officer or equivalent? Is Justrite registered with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, and what does the privacy policy currently say?
How often are backups taken for the website, database and uploaded prescription images? Where are they kept, and when was a restore last tested?
What is your incident process for a data breach, an outage, or a defaced page? Who is called in what order?
What internet connection, devices (PC, tablet, phone), printers and barcode scanners does each store have? Are there stores with unreliable power or data?
What is the process when the internet is down in a store? Can staff continue to serve customers manually and reconcile later?
What monitoring do you want (uptime, errors, slow pages) and who receives alerts?
Which third-party scripts or plug-ins do you want to keep, and which should be dropped?
What are your policies on staff using personal phones and WhatsApp for customer data?
Are there any security audits, penetration tests or compliance reviews we should take into account?
What internal IT support hours and response expectations will staff and managers have after launch?

sections.name: Store managers and store teams
sections.who: Each of the 14 store managers, plus one associate and one pharmacist per store

questions.q: Store name, full address, the phone number customers should call, and the WhatsApp number (if different).
Exact opening hours for each day, public holidays, and any 24-hour service.
Services offered in the store today.
Which of these are free and which are paid?
Is there a private area for consultation? Is there a pharmacist on duty at every opening hour?
How many staff work in each shift?
What are the busiest days and times? What is the slowest period?
Who will check the online orders queue in this store, how often, and who covers if they are busy or off?
How do you receive orders now (phone, WhatsApp, walk-in)? How are they recorded?
How long does it take to pick and pack an average order today? What slows it down?
How are products arranged on shelves? Do you use shelf or bin codes the app should show?
How do you currently handle expiry dates and batch numbers when selling? Who checks them and when?
How often do you count stock and how do you record differences?
What do you do when a product is out of stock or a customer asks for an item you do not carry? Will you transfer from another store?
Is pickup in the store offered? What identification does the customer show and who hands over?
What happens when a customer calls to ask where their order is? Who answers and what system do they use?
Which local landmarks, bus stops and directions help customers find you? Is there parking or accessibility information?
Which local competitors are within 2 km, and what do customers say about them?
Which community groups, churches, mosques, schools, clinics or employers near the store could host a health screening or partnership?
Can we photograph the shopfront, interior and team (with consent)? Who arranges it and when?
What do you want customers to say after visiting? What do they complain about most today?
How are online customer reviews and Google messages handled today for this store?
How do customers pay in store? Which methods and POS terminals?
Who counts and banks the pay-on-delivery cash and how is it reconciled at shift end?
What training have staff had on computers, tablets or apps? Who in the store is the best champion for the new system?
What would make you not use the system on a busy day? Please be honest.

sections.name: Procurement, inventory and supply chain
sections.who: Head of procurement, inventory controller, central warehouse if any

questions.q: Where does the master product list live today (system, spreadsheet)? Who owns it and who may change it?
How many active products (SKUs) do you stock in total and per store? Which are the top 100 sellers?
Which chronic-care medicines (blood pressure, diabetes, others) do you stock in depth, and which generics and brands are available for each?
What data do you hold for each product?
Do you have product photographs? If not, who will supply them?
Who sets prices, how often do they change, and who approves a change? What triggers one?
Can you honour a locked price for 90 days (Chronic Bundle)? What conditions would you need from suppliers?
How do you handle sudden supplier price rises? Who decides whether to absorb them?
Who are your main suppliers and distributors? Payment terms, delivery lead times, minimum orders?
How do you verify a supplier and the genuineness of a batch before accepting it?
What is recorded at goods receiving? Who does it, and is each batch number and expiry date captured?
How do you handle expiry today?
How do you decide reorder quantities? Do you forecast seasonal demand (for example malaria season)?
How often are products out of stock for chronic medicines? Which ones most often?
How are transfers between stores requested, approved, moved and recorded?
How would you find every customer who received a given batch if a recall was announced today?
How do you handle returns from customers and returns to suppliers?
Are there products you will not sell online (restricted, bulky, cold chain, high theft)?
Which stores can serve as fulfilment hubs for online orders in each city?
What stock accuracy do you believe you have today? When was the last full count and what difference did it show?
Who should see cost prices and margins, and who must not?
What reports do you need from the platform each day, week and month?
Which payment methods will be live at launch (pay on delivery, bank transfer, card via Paystack, POS on delivery, others)?
Which bank accounts receive which payments? Who reconciles each one and how often?
How should pay-on-delivery cash and POS be collected, recorded, handed over and banked? Who signs for it?
What cash limits and controls apply to riders and stores?
What is the refund policy by reason (wrong item, damaged, late, unavailable, change of mind, prescription rejected) and the time limit?
Who may approve a refund and up to what amount? How is a refund paid back?
How do you handle failed payments, double payments and chargebacks?
What are the delivery fees and free-delivery thresholds you want at launch? Who approves changes?
How should discounts, coupons, loyalty points and price locks be recorded in the books?
How are prepaid Chronic Bundles and sponsor payments treated: liability, revenue recognition, refunds of unused months?
Do you accept foreign currency payments? Which accounts, rates, and who converts?
What invoices or receipts must the customer get? What tax treatment applies to each product category?
Which accounting software do you use and what must be exported to it?
What approvals are needed before a supplier is paid for stock ordered through the platform?
What financial reports do you want from the admin console?
What audit or tax requirements apply to online sales records?
Who monitors payment-gateway fees and settlement timing?

sections.name: Customer service, WhatsApp and call team
sections.who: Customer service lead, call or WhatsApp agents, store front-desk staff

groups.title: Common questions and the advice boundary

questions.q: Which channels do customers use today (phone, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, email, walk-in)? Who answers each one?
Who owns the main WhatsApp number? How many people use it, from which devices, and how are chats handed over?
What are your published support hours and the response times you can truly meet, on weekdays, weekends and holidays?
What are the ten most common questions or problems?
What do you say and do when a customer asks for medical advice? When does the chat go to a pharmacist?
What may agents never say or promise?
Which languages and styles do customers use? Do agents use Pidgin or local languages, and should the brand voice allow it?
How do you handle an angry customer, a delay, a wrong item, a damaged item, a late delivery?
What should the customer receive proactively (confirmations, delays, dispatch, delivery, refill reminders)?
What compensation or goodwill gestures may agents offer on their own, and above what value must a manager approve?
How are complaints recorded, owned, and closed? How do you check customer satisfaction?
What customer information may be shared over WhatsApp? What must never be sent (for example prescription images in group chats, full addresses)?
How do you ask for and record consent for reminders, marketing and reviews?
How are abusive customers or suspected fraud (fake orders, repeated refusals) handled?
When and how do you ask customers for Google reviews? Who replies to them?
Who monitors social media comments and messages and how quickly do they reply?
What reports do you want on contacts per order, response time, resolution time and top issues?
Do you want an AI-drafted reply assistant? What approvals and limits should apply (the platform's assistant drafts only; a person sends)?
What training do agents need before launch, and who gives it?

sections.name: Delivery and logistics
sections.who: Logistics manager, dispatch lead, rider supervisor, any delivery partner

questions.q: Are riders employees, contractors, or an outside partner? Names of the partners and contacts.
Which areas can you deliver to within 2 hours and within 24 hours, from which stores?
What delivery times can you honestly promise, and what percentage do you meet today?
What are the cut-off times for same-day delivery by store?
How many riders and vehicles are available per store or area? What is the maximum number of orders per hour?
What do you charge or pay per delivery? What does a delivery really cost you, on average?
How are riders chosen, vetted, trained and insured? What is the process for lost or stolen medicine?
How are orders packed? What packaging, tamper seals and labels are used?
What proof of delivery do you require (photo, OTP, signature, call)? How is it linked to the order?
Who is allowed to receive a prescription medicine delivery? What if the patient is not home?
What happens if nobody is home, the address is wrong, or the customer refuses to pay?
How are pay-on-delivery cash and POS handled by riders? How is it settled and audited?
What happens when medicine is damaged or delayed in transit?
Should the customer see the rider's name and phone number? Under what safeguards?
Which products need special handling or are excluded from delivery?
How do you handle deliveries outside Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Osun, or interstate? Which couriers?
What security rules apply to riders and cash in high-risk areas or times?
What do you need from the platform (manifest, route, batch details, scanner) to deliver faster?

sections.name: Marketing, brand and content
sections.who: Marketing lead, social media manager, designer, current agency

questions.q: Please share logo files, colours, fonts and any brand guidelines. Is the platform's teal and type system approved as the brand look?
Do you have a written tagline, mission, values and 'about us' story? Please share them.
What are your current channels and handles?
Who administers each account and what is the posting routine today? What has worked and what has not?
How many followers/subscribers do you have and what content performs best?
What is the story behind 'HealthGist'? Should it become the name of the content programme and newsletter?
Which images and videos do you own and have rights to? Are there professional photographs of stores, products, staff?
What customer testimonials do you have, with written permission to publish?
Who is the primary customer you want to reach with content: chronic-care patients, parents, young adults, diaspora children, employers, HMOs? Rank them.
What health days and seasons matter to your business?
What offers and promotions do you run? Rules, dates, who approves, and legal limits?
What are your rules for influencers, ambassadors or health professionals who speak for Justrite?
Which competitors' content do you admire or dislike? Why?
What topics must we avoid because of regulation, culture, or past incidents?
How do you moderate comments and handle negative or false posts?
What are the approval steps and turnaround times for each content type, and who is the backup?
What is the company's stance on paid advertising for pharmacy products, and who is the contact at the ad platforms?
What events (health screenings, store openings, community drives) are planned in the next 6 months?
Do you have a press list or journalists you have worked with?
What newsletters, bulk SMS or WhatsApp broadcast lists exist, and was consent recorded?
What are your top 10 questions you wish customers asked, and top 10 myths you wish you could correct?

sections.name: HR, training and administration
sections.who: HR lead, admin manager, training lead

questions.q: Please provide the staff structure for head office and the 14 stores (roles, numbers, reporting lines).
Which roles need access to: orders, prescriptions, customer data, stock, prices, refunds, reports, content?
Who requests, approves and removes staff accounts? How fast should leavers lose access?
What training and onboarding exist? How many days would you set aside for training in each store before launch?
What is the best time and format for training (in store, remote, short sessions, shifts)?
Who in each store would be the 'super-user' trainer?
What are the consequences of not following a safety or data rule, and who decides?
Do staff sign confidentiality or data-handling agreements? Please share the template.
What is your policy on staff posting about Justrite on personal social media or LinkedIn? Are staff allowed to be named and photographed?
May pharmacists and managers be asked to join a LinkedIn advocacy programme? Is it voluntary?
What are the staff performance measures that could be linked to the platform (SLA, accuracy, reviews)?
How are new joiners verified (licences, references)? Who keeps the register of professional registrations and their renewal dates?
What languages do staff speak and write well? Is there a need for training in English writing for customer messages?
Are there union, labour-law or working-hour constraints on shifts and on-call tasks?
How do staff report problems or suggest improvements? Who reviews them?

sections.name: Legal, compliance and regulatory
sections.who: Legal adviser / compliance officer / Superintendent Pharmacist

questions.q: Please list every licence and registration.
Which licence numbers and names may be shown publicly, where, and in what wording?
Do all 14 stores have current licences? When does each expire and who tracks renewal?
What rules apply to the sale of prescription medicines through a website, to delivery, and to advertising them? Who has confirmed this in writing?
What are the rules on advertising pharmacy services and health products in Nigeria that apply to us (PCN, NAFDAC, APCON, others)? Is there a pre-approval process?
Who owns the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, when were they last reviewed, and by whom?
How long must prescriptions, dispensing records, delivery records, and patient data be kept? Where?
How do customers exercise data rights (access, correction, deletion, withdrawing consent)? Who answers them and within what time?
What consent wording do you need for health data, reminders, marketing messages and reviews?
May the pharmacy share patient information with a family payer (Sponsor a Parent) and what consent is required?
What international data transfer rules apply to a diaspora payer, cloud hosting and third-party tools?
What contracts do you have with suppliers, HMOs and logistics partners that limit what we can say or do?
What insurance (professional indemnity, product liability, goods in transit, cyber) is in place?
How are regulatory inspections handled and what records must be produced within what time?
Who is the contact at PCN, NAFDAC and NDPC, and what is the status of any open correspondence?
What disclaimers or statements must appear in the footer, product pages and health content?
Is there any pending dispute, complaint or press issue we should know about before publishing?

sections.name: Cross-department questions
sections.who: Everyone — answered once by the project sponsor with input from all

questions.q: Who is the single project sponsor and who is the day-to-day coordinator on Justrite's side?
What are the go / no-go conditions for opening public online ordering? Who signs off?
Which store or stores will pilot first, and why?
How will you decide that the pilot is working? Which numbers, over what period?
What is the escalation path when departments disagree (pharmacy versus sales, store versus head office)?
What meeting rhythm will you keep (daily stand-up, weekly review, monthly steering)?
What is the biggest risk you see in moving the website to the platform?
What would you want to change about how Justrite operates, if the system made it possible?
What did we not ask that we should have?
